title: Ironhollow Rising Revisited
premise: Ulyana Sterling has spent fifteen years guarding the sealed gate at Ironhollow, trading quiet favors with smugglers and pretending the mountain's old court is a fairy story. When a mute child arrives speaking the pre-kingdom tongue of the deep folk, Ulyana realizes the gate's seal is failing and that the child carries a stolen soul — her own brother's, sold to the court beneath the mountain decades ago. To save both the child and what remains of her family, she must descend through the Thornfell roads she knows best and bargain with a court that feeds on debts. She wins the soul back by offering the one thing the court values more: her post as keeper, sealing herself inside so the gate can be closed from beneath — but the child, revealed as the court's true heir, breaks the cycle by unmaking the debt-magic entirely, freeing Ulyana at the cost of the court's power as the long winter finally breaks.
about_author: S. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent years mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy rooted in borders, bargains, and the people who live where maps run out.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A routine winter audit of the Ironhollow gate introduces her world: the seal, the smuggler roads, the ledgers of small favors. She notes a hairline crack in the wardstone and tells no one. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, the comfort of routine beginning to fray.

chapters.title: A Knock Before the Snow
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. On the last passable night, a child of seven or eight arrives alone at the keeper's door, barefoot in the snow, speaking a language older than any kingdom Ulyana knows. The gate's wards hum when the child passes them. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in tenderness.

chapters.title: Words Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with fragments of the child's dream-speech. Using her grandmother's forbidden primer, Ulyana deciphers enough to learn the child's name — Vess — and one phrase repeated like a prayer: 'the debt comes due.' Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: What My Brother Sold
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter, Ulyana's POV. She confronts her memory of Tam, the brother who vanished twenty years ago after borrowing money from the wrong travelers. The primer reveals the court beneath the mountain buys souls against winter. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: Bramble Ostwick's POV, the smuggler who owes Ulyana three favors. He confirms rumors: the deep court has woken, and something is buying passage upward. He agrees to guide her partway for a price she'll hate. Emotional beat: loyalty as currency, and its interest rates.

chapters.title: Leaving the Gate Unkept
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She rigs the wards to hold without her, an act that should be impossible, and descends into Thornfell with Vess and Bramble. The first night below, the mountains answer the child's sleep-talk with answering lights. Emotional beat: crossing the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Vess's POV, rendered in simple, strange prose. The smuggler roads shift around the child; paths she dreamed appear before she walks them. Bramble grows frightened of her. Ulyana chooses to trust. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into unease.

chapters.title: The Hollow Inn
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. Shelter at an inn whose patrons don't blink right. Ulyana trades her mother's ring for information: the court's steward collects debts at midwinter, and Tam Sterling's name is still on the rolls. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Midwinter's Steward
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The steward finds them anyway — courteous, terrible, wearing a face assembled from borrowed features. He offers Vess safe return if Ulyana surrenders her claim on Tam's soul. She refuses. Emotional beat: power's politeness, and its teeth.

chapters.title: Descent Through the Root Roads
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. Fleeing the steward, they take the root roads — passages grown rather than dug. Vess navigates instinctively while Bramble realizes the child isn't lost down here; she's expected. Emotional beat: the dawning sense of walking into a trap laid long ago.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Arrival at the court: a cathedral of roots and debt-ledgers, nobles wearing centuries of bought faces. She sees Tam — alive, hollowed, serving as the court's archivist. He doesn't recognize her. Emotional beat: reunion as heartbreak.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Interest
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, his first. Inside his hollowed mind, fragments surface: the original bargain, the soul he sold to buy medicine for their dying mother, the ledger that never closes. He begins, dimly, to remember Ulyana. Emotional beat: grief for a self already spent.

chapters.title: The Heir Nobody Claimed
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The court recognizes Vess — not as a foundling but as the true heir of the deep throne, hidden above as insurance against the usurper steward. Both factions now want the child. Emotional beat: protectiveness hardening into defiance.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Three Parts
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana negotiates: Tam's soul returned, Vess freed, the gate resealed — in exchange for her keeper's oath transferred below, binding her to the court forever. The steward accepts too readily. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered with open eyes.

chapters.title: Bramble's Choice
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. Offered his debts erased if he betrays their escape route to the steward, Bramble instead burns his own ledger-page, severing the court's claim on him at great pain. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen over survival, at last.

chapters.title: The Ledger Fire
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Restored to half-himself by the first payment of Ulyana's bargain, Tam turns archivist skills against the court, forging entries to void other souls' debts and starting a fire in the record hall. Emotional beat: a hollow man choosing to burn bright.

chapters.title: What the Steward Wanted
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Betrayal revealed: the steward never wanted Vess crowned — he wanted Ulyana's keeper-oath, which anchors the gate's magic, so he could walk through it with an army. Her sacrifice was the weapon. Emotional beat: the corruption of power turning her gift into a knife.

chapters.title: Vess Wakes the Mountain
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Backed against the gate itself, Vess stops hiding. She speaks the pre-kingdom tongue fully for the first time, and the mountain — older than the court, older than the debts — answers her. Emotional beat: the smallest character becoming the largest force.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Breaks
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Climax: Vess unmakes the debt-magic at its root, the court's nobles crumble into the centuries they borrowed, and the steward is claimed by every soul he ever collected. Ulyana's oath dissolves with the ledger it was written in. Emotional beat: catharsis through unmaking.

chapters.title: Two Keepers
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Aftermath below: Tam, mostly himself, chooses to stay as the new keeper of a quieter, honest gate, tending what remains of the deep folk. Ulyana lets him go — the goodbye she never got twenty years ago. Emotional beat: love as letting go.

chapters.title: Thaw at Ironhollow
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She and Vess climb back into late spring. The gate holds, now sealed from both sides by choice rather than fear. Bramble waits with tea and complaints. Emotional beat: exhaustion, relief, the fragile start of a family neither expected.

chapters.title: The Language We Keep
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, closing frame mirroring chapter one. She teaches Vess her grandmother's primer, adding new words: home, stay, sister. The final line reveals Vess's first sentence spoken plainly: 'I was sent to find you.' Emotional beat: quiet hope, debts repaid in love.
